proposal: The Mandate calls Section 702 an essential tool and recommends that Congress review the PCLOB report to decide whether reforms or codification of administrative changes are needed. For traditional FISA it suggests stiffer penalties for leaks aimed at domestic political targets, tighter controls on intercepts that touch domestic political figures, an express bar on politically motivated use, and better DOJ and FISC accountability.

status_summary: Section 702 was reauthorized with a 2026 sunset by Public Law 118-49 (signed 2024-04-20, before the tracking period), which also added query-approval, audit and penalty provisions that overlap with some Mandate safeguards. In 2026 Congress passed short extensions (the last, Public Law 119-87, signed 2026-04-30, moved the Title VII sunset to 2026-06-12); the House then rejected a further extension on 2026-06-11 (198 to 218) and Title VII of FISA, including Section 702, lapsed on 2026-06-12, the first lapse since 2008. Collection was reported to continue under FISC certifications approved in March 2026 that run to about March 2027, and the Senate confirmed Jay Clayton as DNI on 2026-07-28 (sworn in 2026-08-03). As of 2026-07-29 reports said the House was out until 2026-08-31 with no Senate plan to act, and none of the public laws numbered 119-99 through 119-118 (through 2026-09-30) that were checked on govinfo concerns FISA, so no reauthorization and no new Mandate-style traditional-FISA safeguard was found enacted since the lapse.

timeline.event: FISC recertifies the Section 702 program in March 2026 (exact day not confirmed; month-level date); the certifications are reported to run through about March 2027.

After a House five-year renewal with some reforms failed on 2026-04-16 (200 to 220) and a procedural vote on an 18-month clean renewal also failed, Congress passes a short extension to 2026-04-30; the Senate approves it by voice vote.

Public Law 119-87 (S. 4465) is approved, changing the repeal dates in section 403(b) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 from 2026-04-30 to 2026-06-12, so Title VII (including Section 702) is extended to that date.
The House rejects a further short-term extension (H.R. 9238), 198 for and 218 against, a day before the authority was due to expire.

Section 702 and the rest of FISA Title VII lapse at midnight (12 a.m. on 2026-06-13 per CBS), the first lapse since the authority was enacted in 2008; existing certifications are expected to keep collection going.

Punchbowl News reports that the House has left until 2026-08-31, the Senate has no plan to take up reauthorization before its recess, major telecom providers are still sharing data, and large groups of conservative Republicans and progressive Democrats oppose an extension without new warrant protections. The Senate had confirmed Jay Clayton as DNI on 2026-07-28 by a party-line 51 to 47.
ODNI lists the swearing-in of Jay Clayton as Director of National Intelligence, the most recent item on its press-release page; no ODNI release on Section 702 reauthorization appears on that page.

The latest public law found on govinfo, Public Law 119-118, does not concern FISA; public laws 119-99 (2026-06-12) through 119-118 that were checked contain no Title VII extension, so the lapse was still unresolved by statute at that date.

title: Keep FISA Section 702, add accountability reforms, and guard against partisan misuse
uncertainties: The govinfo check covers public laws 119-99 to 119-118 only through the 2026-09-30 law found; govinfo may lag the most recent enactments, and a House or Senate vote after 2026-07-29 would not show up as a public law, so I cannot rule out floor action in September. Searches for August to October 2026 news, including a final search on September 2026 floor action, returned only June and July 2026 items (and a 2024 Senate vote), and a forum timeline of the 2026 reauthorization fight ended on 2026-06-17. The 2026-06-11 vote count (198 to 218) is from the New Jersey Monitor. The Mandate's PCLOB reliance is affected by the January 2025 removal of three PCLOB members (reported in a Berkeley Tech Law Journal article), which I did not verify from a primary source. Whether the lapse has changed provider cooperation beyond the July 2026 reports was not verified.
